# Full Experiment Design — BAdam vs LoRA on Llama-3-70B / MathInstruct / Zero-Shot Math

This is a **design document only**. Nothing has been executed. No installs, no training, no downloads.

---

## 0. One-line answer target

Does BAdam (a memory-efficient full-parameter optimizer) win on zero-shot math over LoRA (parameter-efficient fine-tuning), when both are matched on data, base model, template, decoding, and token budget on Llama-3-70B?

---

## 1. Problem & design rationale

### 1.1 Research question
Will BAdam achieve higher zero-shot math accuracy than LoRA when fine-tuning Llama-3-70B on MathInstruct?

### 1.2 Why the comparison is meaningful
BAdam (Luo et al., ICLR 2024, *BAdam: A Memory-Efficient Full Parameter Optimization of Adam*) and LoRA (Hu et al., 2022) attack two different bottlenecks:
- **LoRA**: keeps activations of the frozen base and trains a low-rank residual. Trainable params O(d·r). Memory is in optimizer state, gradients on the **adapter only**, activations of base.
- **BAdam**: trains **all 70B parameters** but updates only one *block* per optimizer step, computing Adam-like stats on the active block and **frozen first-moment / zero second-moment** for inactive blocks. Memory is dominated by one block's optimizer state + activations, not the full parameter footprint.

Both can fit Llama-3-70B SFT inside 8×80 GB with 4-bit base weights and a careful ZeRO-3 schedule. The question is whether full-parameter SFT (BAdam) recovers enough quality headroom over PEFT (LoRA) in zero-shot math to be preferred, holding everything else constant.

### 1.3 Threats to validity and design-level mitigations

| Threat | Mitigation in this design |
|---|---|
| Different prompt templates favor one arm | Same raw-completion BOS-prefixed prompt, identical system prompt (None) and stop strings for both arms |
| Different decoding confounds | Greedy decoding for `pass@1`; shared sampler for `pass@k` (`temperature=0.7, top_p=0.95`) |
| Decontamination of MathInstruct vs benchmark test items | 8- and 13-gram decontamination filter applied to training set before SFT; offending items dropped and counted |
| Different quantization recipes favor one arm | Both arms use **identical NF4 (4-bit) base weights** + bf16 trainable buffers; LoRA stays in QLoRA form, BAdam in Q-bitsandbytes-compatible form |
| Compute unfairness | Effective batch size and total tokens matched across arms; also log wall-clock so the reader can see any speedup cost |
| Seed-picking by luck | Pre-registered seed sets; 3 seeds for headline cells, **6 seeds only on the single locked-in best config per arm** for the confirmatory CI |
| Incoherent reporting (per-task vs averaged) | Report per-benchmark primary and a clearly-labeled arithmetic mean only as a coarse summary |
| Pre-registered cherry-picking | Locked decision rule in §7 before any training |

### 1.4 Pre-registered pass criterion (headline)
**PASS** iff, on the *confirmatory 6-seed runs* on the locked best config of each arm:
- Δ pass@1 (BAdam − LoRA) is positive **and** the paired bootstrap 95% CI excludes 0 on **at least two** of {GSM8K, MATH, AIME}, **and**
- Δ values are not sign-flipped on a low-variance sanity fallback (GSM8K).

### 1.5 Pre-registered fail / equivalence rule
- **FAIL**: Δ < 0 with 95% CI excluding 0 on GSM8K and AIME **or** Δ < −1.0 pp on MATH.
- **EQUIV** (declare "no robust advantage"): |Δ| ≤ 0.5 pp on GSM8K **and** |Δ| ≤ 1.0 pp on MATH with 95% CIs enclosing 0.

### 1.6 Out of scope
- Inference throughput at fixed accuracy (we report training throughput only).
- RLHF / DPO / RFT second-stage.
- Non-math benchmarks (MMLU, BBH, etc.).
- Multi-node scaling beyond single node.

---

## 2. Treatments (arms)

### 2.1 Arm A — LoRA (PEFT, baseline)
- Adapter injection on **all linear projections in attention and MLP**: `q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj, gate_proj, up_proj, down_proj`.
- Adapter dtype: bf16.
- Base weight dtype: **NF4 (4-bit), double-quant off**, computed via `bitsandbytes`.
- Sweep cells: `r ∈ {16, 64}`, `α = 2·r`, dropout `0.05`. So two cells per arm.
- Optimizer: AdamW on adapter parameters only; betas `(0.9, 0.999)`, weight decay `0.0`, eps `1e-8`.

### 2.2 Arm B — BAdam (memory-efficient full-FT)
- All 70B parameters trainable, base weight NF4 (matched to Arm A).
- Optimizer: BAdam; block size = **layer-wise fine-grained** (each Transformer block's Q/K/V/O/MLP linear forms one block — paper's main recipe).
- Sweep cell: stages-per-step `s ∈ {1, 2, 4}`. Three cells.
- BAdam LR sweep `{5e-6, 1e-5, 2e-5}` chosen by first-pass validation on GSM8K-train-100-sample held-out (also applied to LoRA at LR `{1e-4, 2e-4}` to keep sweeps symmetric in cardinality).

### 2.3 Matched invariants across arms (single source of truth)

| Invariant | Value |
|---|---|
| Base model | `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-70B` (base, **not** Instruct — SFT is what we are measuring) |
| Tokenizer | Meta-Llama-3 tokenizer, BOS-prefixed raw completion format |
| Quantization | NF4 base, bf16 trainable buffers |
| Training data | `TsinghuaC3I/MathInstruct` post-decontamination |
| Optimizer family | Adam-flavored (LoRA: AdamW; BAdam: BAdam) |
| LR schedule | cosine, 3% warmup, 1 epoch |
| Sequence length | 2048 packed |
| Effective batch size | 64 sequences × 2048 tokens = **131,072 tokens / micro-batch**; **gradient accumulation 4 ⇒ 524,288 tokens / optimizer step** |
| Total tokens seen | identical across arms ≈ MathInstruct ~262k × ~1k tokens ≈ **260M tokens** ≈ **~500 optimizer steps** (1 epoch) |
| Seeds per cell | 3 (`{1, 2, 3}`) for sweep |
| Confirmatory seeds | 6 (`{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}`) on best cell of each arm |
| Hardware | 1 node × 8×80 GB A100/H100 |
| Parallelism | FSDP / DeepSpeed **ZeRO-3**; for BAdam, offload inactive blocks to CPU pinned memory with prefetch (CPU offload is a **logged flag**, not default) |
| Precision math | bf16 forward/backward; FP32 master for trainable buffers |
| Random | torch `seed_everything`, deterministic algorithms on where supported; CUDA backend deterministic |

---

## 3. Data

### 3.1 Training data
- Source: `TsinghuaC3I/MathInstruct`. Treat **262k mixed-sample partition** as canonical; subset packaged as `MathInstruct.json` and `MathInstruct.parquet`. Use the *training split* only.
- Tokenize with the Llama-3 tokenizer; pack to `seq_len=2048` with `DataCollatorForLanguageModeling(mlm=False)` and `group_by_length=True`.
- Format: `{"instruction": ..., "input": ..., "output": ...}` → concatenated as `BOS + instruction + input + output + EOS`; loss is computed **only on the `output` tokens** to match standard SFT practice. Same masking for both arms.

### 3.2 Decontamination
- Build n-gram sets of test items from **GSM8K test (1319)**, **MATH test (5000)**, **AIME 2020–2025 (180 problems)**.
- Token 8-grams and 13-grams (whitespace-tokenized).
- For every MathInstruct training item, drop it iff any 13-gram from test items appears; record drops; require post-filter training set to lose **no more than 5%** of items; if > 5%, raise and refine to a 20-gram filter as a fallback.
- Report `n_train_before`, `n_train_after`, drop rate per source benchmark.

### 3.3 Held-out evaluation
- **GSM8K** test split, 1319 items. Answer is a single integer; primary metric is strict exact-match after extraction.
- **MATH** test split, 5000 items; primary metric exact-match with `\boxed{...}` extractor (sympy equivalence on rendered expressions as secondary).
- **AIME** (2020–2025) ≈ 180 items; primary metric exact-match on integer answer; reported but **not** used as a pass-criterion benchmark because of high variance at small N (we do require AIME to be reported; threshold rule is GSM/MATH only).
- **No few-shot exemplars** in any prompt. The single system-level instruction (identical across arms) is left as `None` per the locked prompt choice — pure zero-shot, BOS-prefixed completion.

---

## 4. Training recipe

### 4.1 Tokenization & packing
- Llama-3 BPE; sequence length 2048; packing `Seq2SeqTrainer`'s `group_by_length=True`. Mask the `instruction+input` part of the loss.

### 4.2 Per-arm hyperparameters

**Arm A — LoRA**
| Hyperparam | Value |
|---|---|
| `r` | 16, 64 |
| `lora_alpha` | 2r |
| `lora_dropout` | 0.05 |
| target_modules | q,k,v,o,gate,up,down |
| learning_rate | {1e-4, 2e-4} (3-seed sweep) — best cell locked, then 6-seed confirmatory |
| batch micro | 64 seq × 2048 tok |
| grad accum | 4 |
| warmup | 3% of steps |
| cosine to 0 | yes |
| weight decay | 0.0 on adapters |
| beta1, beta2 | 0.9, 0.999 |
| eps | 1e-8 |
| gradient checkpointing | on |

**Arm B — BAdam**
| Hyperparam | Value |
|---|---|
| block scheme | per-transformer-layer fine-grained |
| stages s | 1, 2, 4 (3-seed sweep) — best s locked, then 6-seed confirmatory |
| learning_rate | {5e-6, 1e-5, 2e-5} (3-seed sweep) |
| batch micro | 64 seq × 2048 tok |
| grad accum | 4 |
| warmup | 3% of steps |
| cosine to 0 | yes |
| beta1, beta2 | 0.9, 0.999 |
| eps | 1e-8 |
| gradient checkpointing | on |
| ZeRO-3 offload of inactive blocks | off (default); **flag** for 1×80 GB fallback |

### 4.3 Parallelism and precision
- DeepSpeed ZeRO-3, `bf16_enabled`, `fp32_master_weights_and_grads`.
- For BAdam: ZeRO-3 partitions parameters; `param_offload=False` by default (all 70B in HBM as fp32 master ≈ 280 GB is too large; therefore BAdam only updates the master for the **active block**, and uses bf16 for the trainable active block only — this is the published BAdam memory model).

### 4.4 Hardware target
8×80 GB A100 or H100, NVLink, single node. **CPU offload is treated as a logged contingency**, not the default.

---

## 5. Decoding & evaluation

### 5.1 Greedy `pass@1`
- Decoding: `do_sample=False`, `temperature=1.0` ignored, `max_new_tokens=2048`, `min_new_tokens=1`, stop on EOS or `\boxed{...}` close + newline.
- Apply **identical post-processing** for both arms: extract the last `\boxed{...}` content; fallback to last integer for GSM8K/AIME; sympy equivalence fallback for MATH.
- Run on every benchmark's full test set.

### 5.2 `pass@k` with sampling
- `temperature=0.7, top_p=0.95, n=8, max_new_tokens=2048`. Estimate `pass@8` unbiased per Chen et al. 2021.
- Also `pass@4` for cost discipline.

### 5.3 Evaluator
- All evaluations go through a single harness (we'll use HuggingFace `lm-evaluation-harness` with `math` task template, or `math_eval` from MathInstruct repo, **whichever is used must be identical for both arms** — choose once, freeze, do not swap mid-experiment).
- Evaluator software version pinned (see §8).

### 5.4 Reporting metrics
- Per benchmark, per arm, per cell:
  - `pass@1` (mean ± std over seeds)
  - `pass@4`, `pass@8`
- Δ pass@1 (BAdam − LoRA), 95% paired bootstrap CI over seeds, 10 000 resamples.

---

## 6. Efficiency / cost reporting

BAdam's claim is *quality at LoRA-like cost*, so this comparison is meaningless without efficiency columns. **Required** for both arms:

| Quantity | How measured |
|---|---|
| Peak GPU memory per GPU (MiB) | `torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated(device)` after warmup and again at step 100, 500, end of step |
| Tokens / optimizer step | identical by design (invariant table) |
| Tokens / sec / GPU | measured over 100 steady steps excluding first 20 warmup |
| Wall-clock to 260M training tokens | from first forward to last evaluation; reported per arm |
| Total CPU offload traffic | bytes transferred CPU↔GPU per step (only BAdam if offload flag is on) |
| EMA snapshot cost | keep last-3 checkpoints, suffix-average pass@1 (reported as `EMA-3` ablation only, **not** as headline) |
| Effective parameter count | LoRA: Σ(r · d_in + r · d_out); BAdam: 70B |

---

## 7. Statistical analysis

- **Confirmatory** statistics use only the 6-seed runs on the **locked best cell** of each arm.
- Per benchmark: `Δ̂ = mean(BAdam_pass@1) − mean(LoRA_pass@1)`, paired by seed.
- 95% CI from 10,000 paired bootstrap resamples.
- Holm–Bonferroni correction across the three benchmarks for the **pass criterion** (GSM8K, MATH, AIME) — applies only to the confirmatory test, not the headline arithmetic mean.
- **Decision rule**:
  - **PASS**: Δ̂ > 0 and CI excludes 0 on at least 2 of {GSM8K, MATH} *after* Holm correction.
  - **FAIL**: Δ̂ < 0 and CI excludes 0 on GSM8K *or* Δ̂ < −1.0 pp on MATH.
  - **EQUIV**: |Δ̂| ≤ 0.5 pp on GSM8K *and* |Δ̂| ≤ 1.0 pp on MATH *and* both CIs include 0.
  - Otherwise, "inconclusive; report all numbers" — no claim either way.

---

## 8. Reproducibility

- Lock `transformers==4.43.x`, `peft==0.11.x`, `trl==0.10.x`, `bitsandbytes==0.43.x`, `accelerate==0.33.x`, `datasets==2.20.x`, `torch==2.4.x`, `deepspeed==0.15.x`, `vllm==0.5.x` (for eval only).
- Random seeds: `{1,2,3,4,5,6}`. Seeds are set in `torch`, `numpy`, `random`, `transformers.set_seed`. `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8` and `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=True)` where supported.
- Base checkpoint SHA pinned: `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-70B` revision id recorded.
- MathInstruct data SHA pinned via `datasets` `download_checksums` or parquet hash recorded.
- Three checkpoints per arm retained (last + 2 best by validation `pass@1` on a 256-item held-out slice of MathInstruct). No test-set hyperparameter selection.

---

## 9. Final result tables (templates to be filled in by the runner)

**Table 9.A — Confirmatory (6-seed, best cell, ± std)**
| | GSM8K | MATH | AIME |
|---|---|---|---|
| LoRA (best cell) | `m±s` | `m±s` | `m±s` |
| BAdam (best cell) | `m±s` | `m±s` | `m±s` |
| Δ̂ (BAdam − LoRA) | `Δ̂ [CI_lo, CI_hi]` | `Δ̂ [CI_lo, CI_hi]` | `Δ̂ [CI_lo, CI_hi]` |

**Table 9.B — Efficiency**
| | Peak GPU mem (GiB) | Tok/s/GPU | Wall-clock to 260M tokens | Offload flag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LoRA (best r) | | | | n/a |
| BAdam (best s) | | | | on/off |

**Table 9.C — Sweep ablation (3 seeds; informational, not confirmatory)**
- LoRA: `r ∈ {16, 64}`, GSM8K pass@1 each.
- BAdam: `s ∈ {1, 2, 4}`, GSM8K pass@1 each.
- Used only to identify the cell that goes into 9.A.

---

## 10. Risks and contingencies

| Risk | Contingency |
|---|---|
| MathInstruct requires HF auth or is rate-limited | Fall back to mirror; in the worst case, use the decontaminated subset from the original WizardMath paper repo (same authors) |
| `deepspeed` + BAdam integration friction | Implement BAdam as a thin "block-frozen Adam" wrapper around `bitsandbytes` 4-bit params + ZeRO-3, replicating the reference paper's release behavior |
| 70B + ZeRO-3 still OOM on a node | Activate CPU offload flag for BAdam only; LoRA unaffected. Log the OOM as a measured finding |
| Evaluation harness gives different answers than expected on small samples | Use sympy equivalence as a secondary metric on MATH and report it as a robustness column, not as a decision column |
| Holm correction kills a marginal PASS | Switch to the un-corrected 95% CI **only** if the researcher pre-approves that relaxation in writing (defer to researcher) |

---

## 11. Decision rule (final, single sentence)

> Report PASS / FAIL / EQUIV / Inconclusive based on the locked pass criterion (§1.4), fail rule (§1.5), and statistical protocol (§7), using only the confirmatory 6-seed runs on each arm's locked best cell — no other statistic, no other cell, and no other seed count is permitted to drive the claim.

---

## Appendix A — Software stack pinned

```
transformers==4.43.x, peft==0.11.x, trl==0.10.x,
bitsandbytes==0.43.x, accelerate==0.33.x, datasets==2.20.x,
torch==2.4.x + CUDA 12.1, deepspeed==0.15.x, vllm==0.5.x (eval only),
numpy==1.26.x, sympy==1.12.x, scipy==1.13.x, scikit-learn==1.5.x
```

The runtime bubblewrap in this design-only phase has **none of these installed and no GPU**; the design above assumes they are installed on the dedicated SFT/eval cluster.

## Appendix B — Items deferred to the researcher

None for the design itself. The next concrete act (execution) requires an HF_TOKEN, a feasible GPU reservation, and pre-approved decontamination thresholds locked.
